core.title: Resolve every implementation testing witness to an identified test
core.given: An implementation source declares one or more testing witnesses
core.when: the implementation testing witnesses are checked for resolution (at any time, regardless of which files changed)
core.then: Each implementation testing witness must resolve to an identified test.
prefer: Point each testing witness at a concrete, identified test that exists, and update the witness in the same change when that test is renamed or moved.
avoid: Leaving a testing witness that names a missing, renamed or ambiguous test.
Creating placeholder or empty tests only so a witness resolves (metric gaming).
core.why: Implementation-to-test links chain with test-to-plan links into plan→test→implementation closure; a dangling witness breaks that chain.
evidence: The traceability-closure check passes for the implementation testing witnesses.
For each testing witness, the referenced test can be located and uniquely identified.
verification: Strict disposition: any unresolved witness is a failure; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.
Repository-wide scope: all implementation testing witnesses are checked, not only those in changed files; pre-existing unresolved witnesses are in scope.
The resolution target is any test of the stack's test inventory, irrespective of the test file's language or kind.
Runs as a validator inside the stack's convention checks; the concrete validator id is a realization detail of the stack.

Presupposes the companion rule that requires testing witnesses to be declared (a witness can only resolve once declared) and runs alongside the companion rule that resolves test bindings; the absence of a witness is not covered here.

values: implementation source declaring a testing witness

fires: Any implementation source in the repository (changed or not) declares a testing witness that names a test not present among the repository's tests.
A test referenced by an implementation testing witness has been renamed, moved or deleted so the witness no longer resolves.
A testing witness points to a test that cannot be uniquely identified.
doesNotFire: An implementation source declares no testing witness (that absence is governed by the companion rule that requires testing witnesses to be declared).
Every implementation testing witness in the repository resolves to an identified test.

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's test runner; the tests it discovers and can uniquely identify are the resolution targets of a testing witness (the core's 'identified test').
The stack's concrete construct by which an implementation source declares a testing witness naming a specific test, so the resolution check can find and parse witnesses.

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's concrete construct by which an implementation source declares a testing witness naming a specific test (comment marker, decorator, annotation), including how the named test is spelled so it can be resolved and uniquely identified.
proposedKeys.bunValue: implementation source declaring a testing witness
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: urn.binding.<artifact> only covers a file binding itself to a URN artifact (component, acceptance, wmbt, ...) and its artifact list has no test kind; no other key in any group describes an implementation source's reference to a test, and the idiom group exists exactly for the stack's concrete construct behind a neutral core concept.

neutralityNotes: Every occurrence of 'Bun test' (title, then, prefer[0], evidence[1], verifier_detail[2], fires) was neutralized to 'test' and instantiates through tooling.test_runner; the obligation is unchanged. The validator id atdd_traceability_closure (verifier_detail[0], evidence[0], fact notes) and the companion rule ids traceability.source.tested-by-present / traceability.test.binding-resolves are ATDD-Bun realization details kept in bunOnly; the core describes the companions generically because their PLT-87 ids are assigned per rule elsewhere. The concrete syntax of a testing-witness declaration has no key in the closed vocabulary, so idiom.testing_witness is proposed and required. 'Implementation source' is already neutral; its mapping to concrete files comes from the stack's shared roles/roots profile data, for which bun.json carries no rule-specific value. The Bun activation-fact notes cannot be carried by the neutral fact schema (fact/values/observability only); their observer-requirement content is preserved via observability=needs_new_observer plus idiom.testing_witness, and the validator-id wording is retained in bunOnly.
